question:
I have table name as rw_ghi_abc. I want to remove rw_ from the table name and for this I am using macro generate_alias_name as :

{% macro generate_alias_name(re,custom_alias_name=none, node=none) -%}
    {%- if custom_alias_name is none -%}
        {{ re.search('g\w+',node.name) }}
    {%- else -%}
        {{ custom_alias_name | trim }}
    {%- endif -%}
{%- endmacro %}

I am using re.search so that I can skip rw_ from the name, after dbt run it gives an error as:

title: change table name dynamically using a macro generate_alias_name in DBT
answer:
Have you imported the re module as {%- set re = modules.re -%}?

Have you tried handling the cases when there is no match?

I think using re.sub, instead of re.search, would be more generic in seamlessly handling any case where the expected pattern is not matched... 🤷

Something like:

{% macro generate_alias_name(re,custom_alias_name=none, node=none) -%}
    {%- if custom_alias_name is none -%}
        {{ modules.re.sub('^rw_', '', node.name) }}
    {%- else -%}
        {{ custom_alias_name | trim }}
    {%- endif -%}
{%- endmacro %

Please note that this solution does not support the recent(ish) handling of model versions, please refer to the core generate_alias_name implementation to see how it's handled there.
